figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)
issue: Internally contradictory threshold claim: the in-figure annotation and the caption both assert that the N-1 residual 'clears the burst only at rho = 1', which is false given the same annotation's own threshold 'need >= 0.917'.
evidence: Annotation text: 'N-1 clears the burst only at rho=1: at rho=0.85 the residual ~= ~5.1 < ~5.5, need >= 0.917'. Caption repeats: 'the N-1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s) clears the burst only at rho = 1'. Independent recomputation: residual = 3 x 2.0 x rho clears 5.5 iff rho >= 5.5/6.0 = 0.9167, so rho = 0.92, 0.95, or 1.0 all clear it (e.g., 3 x 2.0 x 0.95 = 5.7 > 5.5). The figure therefore states a universal-sounding restriction ('only at rho = 1') that its own adjacent number falsifies. Benign-reading challenge: no denominator/population reading makes 'only at rho = 1' true; the strongest charitable reading is 'the printed ~6.0 line is drawn at rho = 1', which is not what the clause says.
acceptance_test: Reword both the annotation and the caption to a correct statement, e.g. 'N-1 clears the burst only for rho >= 0.917 (it fails at rho = 0.85)' or 'the ~6.0 residual holds only at rho = 1; at rho = 0.85 the residual ~= 5.1 < 5.5'. Grep the manuscript for 'only at' combined with 'rho' / 'burst' and confirm no remaining instance asserts rho = 1 is the sole clearing value.

figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)

evidence: Y-axis label reads 'load / capacity (req.s^-1)'; title reads 'small ~5.5 req/s burst'; legend reads 'offered load (burst)' with values in req/s; caption uses 'req/s' throughout (e.g., '~5.5 req/s burst', '~2.0 req/s analytical bound').
acceptance_test: Standardize the axis label to 'load / capacity (req/s)' (or convert all other occurrences to req.s^-1); visual re-inspection shows one rate notation for this figure and its caption.

evidence: Annotation: 'at rho=0.85 the residual ~= ~5.1 < ~5.5'. Caption: '3 x 2.0 x 0.85 approx 5.1 req/s'. Exact value is 5.1, so a single operator (or none) suffices.
acceptance_test: Annotation reads 'the residual ~5.1 < ~5.5' (one operator) and matches the caption's operator choice; re-render confirms.

evidence: The axis ticks are 0–12 req/s and the legend separately identifies offered load and capacity lines; the caption calls each capacity line an 'ideal ρ = 1 analytical service ceiling'. A reader can misread the axis as dimensionless load/capacity.
acceptance_test: Relabel the axis 'requests/s (load or capacity)' or 'req s^-1 (load or capacity)' and re-render; verify no reader can interpret the axis as a dimensionless ratio.

acceptance_test: Move the annotation/arrow to the burst peak, or reword it to 'one host cannot meet load above ~2.0 req/s' and point to the crossing with the one-host bound.

issue: Figure annotations, legend, and axis tick labels are below the 8 pt print floor and will be difficult to read at final trim size.

figure: Figure 17.1 (Sizing a fleet of one model)
issue: Self-contradiction between the in-figure top-right annotation and the caption: both state the N-1 residual 'clears the burst only at ρ = 1' while simultaneously giving a break-even threshold of 'need ≥ 0.917' / 'ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it'. If 0.917 is the threshold, the residual also clears at ρ = 0.95, so 'only at ρ = 1' is literally false and overstates the fragility of the reserve (a skimmer could conclude the 4th host is useless unless efficiency is exactly 100%).
evidence: Top-right block: 'N-1 clears the burst only at ρ = 1: at ρ = 0.85 the residual = ~5.1 < ~5.5, need ≥ 0.917.' Caption caveat: 'the N−1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s) clears the burst only at ρ = 1 — at ρ = 0.85 it is 3 × 2.0 × 0.85 ≈ 5.1 req/s, below the ~5.5 burst (ρ ≥ 0.917 is needed to clear it)'. The arithmetic (5.5/6.0 = 0.9167) is correct; only the 'only at ρ = 1' phrasing contradicts it.
acceptance_test: Reword both the in-figure annotation and the caption so the stated condition is the break-even value, e.g. 'at the ideal ρ = 1 the N-1 residual (6.0) clears the 5.5 burst with 0.5 margin; the break-even is ρ ≈ 0.917, so any efficiency loss below that breaks failover'. Confirm no remaining clause asserts the residual works exclusively at ρ = 1.

Re-render and confirm legibility at print size.

figure: FIGURE 17.1 — Sizing a fleet by burst peak, headroom and failover
issue: The legend label for the 6.0 req/s line contradicts the in-chart annotation for the same line. Legend reads "N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)"; the annotation on the line reads "N-1 residual (~6.0 ideal, ρ = 1)"; the caption reads "the N-1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s)". A reader who takes the legend literally reads "N = 1 residual" as one host's residual capacity (2.0 req/s), not the three-host fleet after one drain (6.0 req/s). The figure therefore labels the same quantity two incompatible ways.
evidence: Rendered page 298: legend row 2 right column = "N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)"; in-plot red text at y≈6.0 = "N-1 residual (~6.0 ideal, ρ = 1)". Caption: "Caveat: the N-1 = 3 residual (~6.0 req/s) clears the burst only at ρ = 1". Arithmetic confirms 6.0 = 3 hosts x 2.0 req/s, i.e. the N-1 fleet, not one host.
acceptance_test: Legend entry is changed to "N-1 residual (3 hosts after 1 drain, ~6.0, ideal)" (or equivalent), and a grep of the figure source confirms the string "N = 1 residual" no longer appears anywhere in Fig 17.1.

figure: FIGURE 17.1 — Sizing a fleet by burst peak, headroom and failover
issue: The in-chart annotation "N-1 clears the burst only at ρ = 1: ρ = 0.85 the burst is ~3.1, need ~0.91" cannot be reconciled with the caption's own arithmetic. The caption states "at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 2.0 x 0.85, 5.1 req/s, below the ~5.5 burst (p >= 0.917 is needed to clear it)". Two candidate defects: (a) the figure's "~3.1" appears to be a typo for "5.1" (3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.1); (b) the figure's "need ~0.91" truncates the true threshold 0.9167 to a value that does NOT clear the burst (0.91 x 6.0 = 5.46 < 5.5). Either way the figure and its caption state different numbers for the same failover threshold. Confidence: medium — the glyphs were read from a 150 dpi render and "5.1"/"3.1" are not separable at this resolution, so the source string must be checked.
evidence: Rendered page 298, in-plot gray annotation, second line: "ρ = 0.85 the burst is ~3.1, need ~0.91". Caption, final sentences: "at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 2.0 x 0.85, 5.1 req/s, below the ~5.5 burst (p >= 0.917 is needed to clear it)". Recomputation: 3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.10; 5.5 / 6.0 = 0.9167.
acceptance_test: Source string for the Fig 17.1 annotation is checked against the caption; the figure prints "5.1 req/s" and "need ~0.92" (or "0.917"), and a recomputation of 6.0 x 0.917 = 5.50 >= 5.5 is shown to hold. If the figure's value is genuinely 3.1, the caption is corrected instead and the discrepancy is explained.

figure: FIGURE 17.1 — Sizing a fleet by burst peak, headroom and failover (caption)
issue: The caption's sizing formula is not reproducible as printed: "the same formula gives N_min = ceil(ρ · 8.6) = 23 for the canonical pack, 22 with the reserve case (iii)". With ρ = 1 (the caption's own stated operating point) ceil(1 x 8.6) = 9, not 23; no ρ <= 1 yields 23. The figure's own basis (2.0 req/s per host) implies N_min = ceil(λ / (2.0 ρ)), which also does not produce 23 from 8.6. The reader is given a formula and a result that cannot both be true, and the figure's own capacity lines (2.0 / 6.0 / 8.0) do not bridge the gap.
evidence: Rendered page 298 caption: "N_min = ceil(ρ · 8.6) = 23 for the canonical pack, 22 with the reserve case (iii) (Chs. 17-20)". Figure: "one host ~2.0 req/s", "N-1 residual (~6.0 ideal, ρ = 1)", "N = 4 fleet (3 working + 1 reserve, ~8.0, ideal)". Recomputation: ceil(0.85 x 8.6) = 8; ceil(1.0 x 8.6) = 9. A benign reading exists (the canonical pack's per-host rate may differ from the figure's illustrative 2.0 req/s), but the caption never states it, so the number is unreproducible either way.
acceptance_test: The caption prints the complete expression including the canonical offered load and the canonical per-host rate (e.g. N_min = ceil(λ / (C ρ)) with λ and C stated), and substituting the stated values reproduces 23 (and 22 for the reserve case). A reader can reproduce both numbers from the caption alone.
